skill.name: set-up-woocommerce-meta-advanced-matching
skill.description: Set up and verify Meta Advanced Matching for WooCommerce through Product Metrics. Check consent and paid-order delivery to an existing Meta Conversions API destination.
skill.summary: Verify consent and live WooCommerce order delivery for Meta Advanced Matching.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance alerts point to product documentation or scoped application steps, and most backticks mark Markdown, not shell execution. The review confirmed risks from authenticated writes, order access, the remote MCP endpoint, and an unpinned installer. It also identified unsafe token handling and consented data sharing that can begin without a separate merchant review.

remediation.issue: Meta access tokens may enter the assistant session
remediation.suggestion: Require direct entry in the Product Metrics app or an approved secret-entry control. Remove instructions to ask for tokens in chat or pass them through command text.

remediation.issue: Saving the Meta destination starts data sharing without a separate matching switch
remediation.suggestion: Before enabling delivery, show the target pixel, data fields, and consent requirements. Ask the merchant to confirm before enabling live delivery or placing a paid test order.

remediation.issue: Prerequisite setup can trigger a historical order import
remediation.suggestion: Keep the import out of the default matching workflow. Explain which data goes to Product Metrics and request separate approval before starting it.

remediation.issue: Authenticated tools can read order details or change production settings
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace, store, and permitted actions before using tools. Request only required fields and require approval for changes before applying retry rules.

remediation.issue: The installation command does not pin the installer or skill revision
remediation.suggestion: Document a user-run installation path with a verified installer version and a reviewed skill revision. Never run the installer as part of setup.

remediation.issue: The MCP fallback relies on a remote service and broad execution interface
remediation.suggestion: Use only the user-approved connector. Restrict enabled operations and workspace permissions to those needed for the requested check.

content.user_title: Set Up Meta Advanced Matching for WooCommerce
content.value_statement: When Meta cannot match store purchases to ad clicks, attribution can be incomplete. Check your Product Metrics setup, confirm consent settings, and verify live order delivery.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP integration to identify incomplete steps.
Guide you in checking whether the existing Meta pixel destination is connected and enabled.
Guide you in selecting a supported consent banner and clearing the full-page cache after changes.
Distinguish a connection test from verifying delivery with a new paid test order.
Explain which matching fields are hashed, which are sent unhashed, and when Meta cookie identifiers are included.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro, a connected WooCommerce store, and a working Meta Conversions API destination.
You complete steps in WordPress and Meta; this workflow does not set campaign bids or optimize campaigns.
Product Metrics does not send Meta events without ad user data consent.
It does not backfill historical orders to Meta, revise sent events after refunds, or guarantee a higher Event Match Quality score.

use_cases.title: Check matching readiness
use_cases.description: Find out whether the store and Meta pixel are connected and which setup steps still need attention.

use_cases.title: Investigate low Event Match Quality
use_cases.description: Check consent configuration and order delivery before investigating which customer signals Meta receives.

use_cases.title: Verify delivery after a consent change
use_cases.description: Check the configured banner, clear the full-page cache, and verify delivery with an approved paid test order.

prompt_templates.title: List setup requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need before checking Meta Advanced Matching on my WooCommerce store? Give me a checklist without connecting to my accounts.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are checking whether your store is ready.

prompt_templates.title: Check existing setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for the Product Metrics store and property I approve. Tell me which items are incomplete without changing settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Your store and Meta pixel may already be connected.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a delivery test
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to test the Meta connection and verify a paid test order. Tell me what confirms each check before I place the order.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to verify live order delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose missing purchase events
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me check consent, paid order status, event age, and the selected pixel. Use read-only checks and do not request tokens or raw customer data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Some paid orders are missing from Meta reporting.

output_examples.input: The connection test passed. Is live order delivery verified?
output: The test confirms that Meta accepts the connection test event.
For live delivery, select Verify with next paid order in WordPress and pay for an approved test order within ten minutes.
Select Refresh connection status and check that Live order delivery reads Verified.

output_examples.input: Does this send only hashed customer information?
output: No. Billing details and the WooCommerce customer ID are hashed when available.
Meta also receives the visitor's IP address and user agent without hashing.
Meta cookie identifiers require ad storage consent, and the event requires ad user data consent.

best_practices: Verify the selected store, property, and Meta pixel before testing or changing settings.
Enter access tokens directly in the designated app field and keep them out of assistant conversations.
After changing the consent banner setting, clear the full-page cache and verify delivery with an approved test order.
anti_patterns: Assuming a connection test proves delivery for paid orders.
Disabling consent checks to make more conversions appear in Meta.
Starting a historical order import just to verify Advanced Matching.

faq.question: Is there a separate switch for Advanced Matching?
faq.answer: No. When the Meta destination is enabled, Product Metrics includes available matching fields on events with ad user data consent.

faq.question: Which consent banners are supported?
faq.answer: The guide lists OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, and Osano. Clear the full-page cache after changing the configured banner.

faq.question: What happens without ad user data consent?
faq.answer: Product Metrics does not send the event to Meta. An unconfigured banner is treated as no consent.

faq.question: Can I keep my existing Meta browser pixel?
faq.answer: Yes. Meta counts matching browser and server events once when they share an event name and ID within 48 hours.

faq.question: Are older orders or later refunds sent to Meta?
faq.answer: Product Metrics does not backfill historical orders to Meta. Later refunds and cancellations do not revise events already sent.

faq.question: Does this guarantee a higher Event Match Quality score?
faq.answer: No. The workflow helps verify the setup and delivery. Meta determines the score from the signals it receives.
